work: Amazon Web Services — Types of governance drift
scope_note: Official use for AWS-managed OUs, accounts, landing zones, controls, policies, and inherited baselines; explicitly excludes resource drift within a baseline.

work: Ramesh Marella — A Standardized Multi-Cloud Governance Model for Policy Consistency and Drift Detection
scope_note: Central policy abstraction, cross-cloud mapping, and continuous policy/configuration drift detection; no deployment-specific activated approval basis described.

work: Thi-Yen Do et al. — AI governance drift: Why audit and governance controls fail after AI deployment
scope_note: AI-specific organizational and behavioral construct evaluated with a survey/PLS-SEM model; not a cloud workload state-to-admission join.

work: Steffen Höpfner and Sigurd Schacht — Architecture as Governance: Why LLM Agents Need Structural Compliance Enforcement
scope_note: Uses socio-technical governance drift for longitudinal erosion of compliance in human–AI teams; different unit of analysis.

work: Oleg Solozobov — Label-Free Detection of Governance Evidence Degradation in Risk Decision Systems
scope_note: Monitors statistical evidence sufficiency for deployed risk models under delayed labels; complementary evidence domain, not immutable cloud admission lineage.

work: Yuxiang Peng and Xiaodi Wu — Stateful Governance for Concurrent Agentic Systems
scope_note: Formalizes stale authorization and approval between request and effect commit; closest temporal neighbor, but its protected interval ends at commit rather than monitoring post-admission deployment drift.

work: NIST SP 800-128 — Guide for Security-Focused Configuration Management of Information Systems
scope_note: Establishes controlled baselines and approved/documented change history; corrects the claim that all configuration management uses only current desired state.

work: Jon Howell and David Kotz — End-to-End Authorization
scope_note: Carries authority that justifies a request across system boundaries; not a post-admission temporal conformance relation.

work: Kiran-Kumar Muniswamy-Reddy et al. — Layering in Provenance Systems
scope_note: Integrates provenance across abstraction layers; supplies lineage architecture but not governance verdict semantics.

work: Wenchao Zhou et al. — TAP: Time-aware Provenance for Distributed Systems
scope_note: Represents time, distributed state, and state changes in provenance; supplies temporal explanation rather than a normative admitted-basis test.

work: Sachin Admane and Tejas Admane — Interpreting risk drift in construction projects: a fuzzy–Bayesian decision framework for weak signal–based governance
scope_note: Construction-project risk governance; neither software deployment governance nor the target decision object.

work: Robert Gordon Spencer — Ethical Drift in Higher Education Leadership: Discretion Silence and Informal Authority in Institutional Governance
scope_note: Institutional ethics and leadership; outside software and cloud systems.

work: João Gama et al. — A survey on concept drift adaptation
scope_note: Statistical change in the relation between inputs and targets; retained only as a terminological false friend.
